## Learning outcome

Explain the role of a majority in a three-node consensus group.

::: {.notes}
Prerequisites: Lectures 05–06. This is a sample deck for the proposed syllabus, not a full lecture.
:::

## Worked scenario

Three registration metadata nodes split into a connected pair and one isolated node. The pair can make progress once a suitable leader is established.

::: {.notes}
Consensus lets participating nodes agree on decisions despite some failures. In Raft, a three-node group uses a majority of two. A node isolated from the other two cannot commit a new log entry by itself.
:::

## Discussion and recap

Why should the isolated node avoid accepting independent committed updates?

**Takeaway:** Agreement and progress are separate properties; a partition can prevent progress for some nodes.

::: {.notes}
Ask students to name assumptions before proposing a solution. The complete planned scope is recorded in the lecture brief.
:::
